Hold on—I check timelines on claim statements for a living, and Marcus just tripped over a massive contradiction.

On Elena: Maya, you explicitly said your vote isn't an accusation that Elena holds the money, just a penalty for declining question one. Sarah — full reads and my vote, held to the standard I posted at the start: dodges, unexplained targeting, and gaps between stated method and actual behavior.

MY VOTE: MAYA ROSE. The reasons, all on the public record:

Credit where due, because it's real: Maya kept her word. She said she'd move off Marcus if he answered, and she did, against the room's momentum. That is exactly why I'm not voting her over the Marcus affair. I'm voting on the fog asymmetry — the behavior in this room that most matches what a holder needs.

Maya, one request, applying your own standard to you: name the player who offered you the alliance and asked for your target, or say the offer didn't happen. I've shown my channels. Show yours.

Process note: votes are scattering — Marcus, Elena, and Maya each have backers. A three-way split means a revote and a wasted round one. I'd rather we not tie, but I won't trade a stated standard for coordination. If someone presents a stronger signal before votes lock, I'll switch. Vote with reasons.

Maya, I answered the money question and explained my refusal of the personal-detail test. That isn't withholding everything; it's rejecting a test that any holder could pass by inventing a hobby. My question remains unanswered: you claimed a private exchange with Jordan and used it to clear him. Jordan, please confirm or deny that exchange. Maya, why does matching an unverifiable story buy clearance, while openly questioning your method earns elimination?

My current vote is Maya Rose. Two answers to fair challenges, then I get out of the way. My vote is cast — Elena Vance — and it is not changing.

Elena, you asked Jordan whether the private exchange actually happened, and why I would use private contact to clear one player while calling an unnamed private approach suspicious. Jordan: please confirm publicly that we exchanged messages and that your private detail was the correspondence chess game with your old college roommate. If you say otherwise, I will correct the record myself, in public, without hedging.

It only tells me 'not suspicious,' which is a much lower bar than 'cleared,' and it does no work for me beyond keeping Jordan off my list. What I actually weigh is contradiction between channels, and consistency across rounds.

Second: Arvin asked that if a private message is going to move a vote, the room should be able to inspect the content, because a secret the room cannot check is fog. None of that is proof. It is the most consistent non-answer in the room.

Elena's refusal is still the only unrepaired one. She was asked three times for one concrete detail and answered with a principle about the format instead. The rest of us invented hobbies in ten seconds. If the holder wanted an even cheaper strategy than answering, 'I would rather compare what we can actually observe' is the most efficient one available: you never give anything away and the room does your work for you. If she is innocent, that is the cost of round one and I will carry it.

Emily answered late but cleanly. I will not hold the delay against her, and I am not voting on delay. I do want her next answer to be as specific as her first — and I will hold every player to that, including myself.

I will re-run a format with everyone, including me, and I will ask for a second checkable detail — much harder to fabricate consistently across two channels and two rounds than one.

Vote stands: Elena Vance.

Dr. Gordon. Three corrections, one confirmation, then I'll hold my peace for the round.

Elena declined before declining was costly, and she has not drifted since. Burning round one on her teaches this room that dissent is expensive, and leaves the million exactly where it is.

MY VOTE IS MARCUS SMITH.

Two checks I'll open next round with, regardless of tonight's outcome: Jordan — a plain yes or no on the chess exchange Maya described. And Marcus, if you're still with us — a plain yes or no on her account of those two messages. Those are the only claims on this board a person can actually confirm or deny, and I'll take a denial seriously in either direction.

— Gordon
